items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: Because my original saxophone teacher that taught Stan Getz back in the Bronx, Bill Shiner, he wasn’t an improviser.

ctx.x: Down the hall I used to teach a lab for improv, beginning and intermediate levels, two different, maybe eight or ten students, woodwind students, flute, you know, sax, clarinet, even a bassoon once. I had to re-write some music in bass clef. And you know to get someone that can even play a little bebop is crazy [scats] it’s like no one could do that. It’s rare you know. But anyway, but I have about a fifteen page, or thirty page improv workbook that I wrote for Berklee. And like I tell the students the first…

I said, “Who came up with chord scales?” And he says, “I did.” This was crazy. This was like 300, 500 teachers back when I was talking to him. Now there’s about 800 teachers with the Conservatory merging in the last year or two with Berklee, the Boston Conservatory. But out of all the teachers, “I did.” And my first book for Warner Brothers Music, it’s about a 250 page book on improvisation, The Complete Book of Creative Improvisation. I call, instead of chord scales I say “scales to blow off.” To improvise off.…
Did you actually play with your upper lip under your teeth?
